note: Budgets are a RATCHET against ACCIDENTAL bloat, not a hard product limit. Raise them
deliberately when a release adds real user-facing surface; never raise them to make a red
gate go away. check-bundle-size.mjs reads only `bundles[*].from/exports/maxRawBytes/
maxGzipBytes`, so this `note` key is inert (JSON carries no comments).
RAISED FOR 1.9.0 SPRINT 2 (ergonomics + parity). Measured, minified, tree-shaken:
core  126275 B raw / 39362 B gzip   (was: limits 120000 / 37000; Sprint 1 measured 36880 gzip)
edge  114981 B raw / 36049 B gzip   (was: limits 110000 / 34000; Sprint 1 measured 33722 gzip)
Overshoot vs the old limits: core +5.2% raw / +6.4% gzip, edge +4.5% raw / +6.0% gzip —
proportionate to the features, with no single module dominating.
What grew (all of it reachable from the measured entry points, which pull only
streamChat/generateText/generateObject/createClient — `tool()`, `filePart()` and
`getModelCapabilities` are tree-shaken OUT of these numbers, so the growth is orchestration):
- timeout layers: resolveTimeouts + createStepTimeout + withAbortReason (core/timeout.ts),
threaded through core/inference.ts and inference/stream-tool-loop.ts
- StreamChatResult.consume() / StreamObjectResult.consume() drain paths (3 sites)
- prompt/instructions canonicalization + the G2 failed-result shells (generate.ts,
core/normalize.ts) and the input-shape XOR guard
- per-call capability overrides: the finalize/apply merge site (core/registry.ts) and the
per-call descriptor clone (internal/config-symbol.ts)
- per-tool timeouts in inference/loop-shared.ts
- document (PDF) input mapping across all four wires (internal/image.ts + 4 adapters)
- Sprint 1 parity work also lands in this build (readDeuzStream HTTP-error part, the
verify wire part, unknown-tool self-healing, the object-shared loop-option guard)
New limits carry ~10% forward headroom so the ratchet still trips on unintended growth:
openai-provider is untouched (596 B raw / 303 B gzip against 1000 / 600) — the provider
factories must stay near-zero, and that budget is the assertion that they do.
ADDED FOR 1.9.0 SPRINT 3 (UI layer): the `chat` and `ui` bundles. Sprint 3 landed ~10 KB raw
of new reachable code (ordered UIMessagePart projection, canonicalFromUI, ChatInput +
filesToImageParts, validateChatRequest, writeData id/transient) and the gate measured ZERO
growth — because every one of those lives on the ./chat and ./ui subpaths, which the core and
edge entries do not reach, so all of it tree-shook away. The whole release could have doubled
these two surfaces without tripping anything. Measured now, same pipeline:
chat  15364 B raw / 5009 B gzip   ->  limits 17000 / 5500  (+10.6% / +9.8% headroom)
ui     9593 B raw / 3949 B gzip   ->  limits 10600 / 4350  (+10.5% / +10.2% headroom)
(These are the numbers check-bundle-size.mjs reports for the export sets below; an earlier
hand measurement over a wider export list read ~25% higher, which would have left the
ratchet ~37% of slack — enough to hide a real regression. Always take the pipeline's number.)

`./observe` just gained renderRunReport — ~18.6 KB raw / 6.9 KB gzip of INLINE HTML/CSS/JS
template that minifies badly (template strings do not compress like code). Neither surface was
measured before, and Sprint 3 already showed what that costs: it shipped ~10 KB with ZERO ratchet
coverage. Both measured through this same pipeline:
otel     18907 B raw / 5839 B gzip  ->  limits 21000 / 6500   (+11.1% / +11.3% headroom)
observe  25269 B raw / 9433 B gzip  ->  limits 27800 / 10400  (+10.0% / +10.2% headroom)
core and edge are UNAFFECTED (+0 B): renderRunReport is not re-exported from src/edge.ts, and the
otel re-export that IS there tree-shakes out of the measured export set — verified byte-identical.
